issues.body:
registry_selftest_gate now passes `$tree_env_requirements` — parsed verbatim out of the CANDIDATE tree's worker-live.sh — into `_selftest_env_blocked`, which splits each row and calls `_selftest_dep_present "$kind" "$probe"`. For kind `pymodule` that sink is:

    python3 -c 'import importlib.util,sys; sys.exit(0 if importlib.util.find_spec(sys.argv[1]) else 1)' "$probe"

Two facts combine. (1) `importlib.util.find_spec(name)` IMPORTS the parent package when `name` contains a dot (documented behaviour) — it is not a pure lookup. (2) For `python3 -c`, sys.path[0] is `''`, i.e. the current directory, and the gate's cwd is the candidate repo root (`tree_scripts="$PWD/scripts"`).

So a candidate diff containing `evil/__init__.py` at the repo root plus one row `X|pymodule|evil.sub|...` in its own SELFTEST_ENV_REQUIREMENTS executes `evil/__init__.py` at scripts/worker-live.sh:2371, in the host worker lane, BEFORE `run_enrolled_selftest` is ever reached — so outside the `gh` PATH shim, in the lane this file itself documents as carrying ambient `gh` credentials (see the comment at ~line 1299 and the three measured production-write incidents at ~line 1115). A top-level `evil/` path is also classified into NOTHING by `_registry_selftest_targets`, so the `direct == #targets` invariant does not notice it.

The new reader deliberately parses rather than sources — the right instinct — but then applies no shape validation whatsoever beyond `not matches[0].strip()`, so the probe argument is unconstrained attacker text. The sink is pre-existing; this diff is what makes its input untrusted, which is the whole point of the change and therefore in scope for it.
issues.fix_hint:
Constrain the candidate table where it is parsed, and/or close the sink:
1. In `_selftest_env_requirements_from_script`, validate every row before printing it: exactly 4 `|`-separated fields, `kind` in a fixed allow-list (`command`, `pymodule`), `probe` matching `^[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_-]*$` (NO dots — that alone removes the parent-import path), non-empty label. Refuse (rc 1) otherwise, so a malformed candidate table fails the gate closed instead of being executed.
2. Independently harden the probe: `python3 -P -c ...` (or `-I`, or `PYTHONSAFEPATH=1`) removes the cwd from sys.path so a repo-root package is not importable even if a dotted name slips through. Belt and braces — do both.
3. Add self-tests that are non-vacuous in the blocking direction: a candidate table row with a dotted pymodule probe (and one with a bad kind, and one with the wrong field count) must REFUSE at the reader, plus a fixture proving `_selftest_dep_present pymodule pkg.sub` does not execute a repo-root `pkg/__init__.py` (e.g. have the fixture's __init__ write a marker file and assert the marker is absent).
issues.title: Candidate-controlled requirement table reaches importlib.find_spec, giving UNSANDBOXED code execution in the worker lane before the suite runs

issues.body:
The stated goal is that every input describing the suite under test comes from the tree under test, so that 'a new dependency row must be preflighted immediately'. But `_assert_worker_image_gate_deps "$name" "$tree_env_requirements"` still resolves each row through the ORCHESTRATOR's `_selftest_requirement_apt_package` (scripts/worker-live.sh:1818), whose case arm is a closed two-entry list (`command|jq`, `pymodule|yaml`) and returns 1 for anything else.

Consequence: a legitimate PR that adds a dependency row, teaches containers/worker-model.Dockerfile to install it, AND teaches the mapper cannot pass the local gate — the Dockerfile lane refuses with 'worker model image final stage does not provision every SELFTEST_ENV_REQUIREMENTS dependency', which misattributes the cause (the image DOES provision it; the orchestrator's mapper simply does not know the row). Behaviour is fail-closed, so this is not a security hole, but the diagnostic is wrong and the half-migration leaves one policy input on the orchestrator revision without saying so.
issues.fix_hint: Either derive the mapping from the target tree too (parse the candidate's `_selftest_requirement_apt_package` case arms the same way the requirement table is parsed), or — simpler and honest — distinguish the two failure modes: when `_selftest_requirement_apt_package` refuses a row, emit a distinct message naming the UNKNOWN ROW ('requirement row <label> has no package mapping in this orchestrator revision') rather than the 'image does not provision' message, and document in the gate's #1576 comment that the kind->package mapping is deliberately orchestrator-side.
issues.title: kind->package mapper stays on the ORCHESTRATOR revision, so the change's own motivating scenario still cannot pass the gate

issues.body:
`#1576 wiring: the gate no longer provisions from the ORCHESTRATOR actionlint pin` (line 4321) is correctly paired with `legacy_actionlint_body` at 4323-4325, which proves the detector pattern actually matches the pre-change shape. The two sibling negative assertions have no such control:
  * line 4319-4320, `grep -c '"$SELFTEST_ENV_REQUIREMENTS" "$SCRIPT_DIR"'` == 0
  * line 4329-4331, `grep -Fc '_assert_worker_image_gate_deps "$name" ||'` == 0
Both patterns are matched against `declare -f` output, which re-renders line continuations and normalises inter-word spacing. If bash's deparser ever emits a different spacing/quoting for either site, the assertion silently becomes always-true and stops detecting a revert to the orchestrator inputs — precisely the always-green failure mode `legacy_actionlint_body` exists to rule out, and the same class of hole the DISPATCH pin comment at ~line 1295 was written about.

Related smaller gap: `_selftest_env_requirements_from_script`'s docstring claims it refuses MISSING definitions, but no row exercises a file that contains no `SELFTEST_ENV_REQUIREMENTS=` line at all, nor a nonexistent path (the `[[ -f ]]` guard).
issues.fix_hint: Add a `legacy_*_body` literal for each of the two remaining negative assertions (a one-line string in the pre-change shape) and assert the same grep returns 1 against it, exactly as line 4323-4325 does. Add two rows to the reader tests: a fixture with no SELFTEST_ENV_REQUIREMENTS line, and `_selftest_env_requirements_from_script "$tmp/no-such-file.sh"`, both expected to print `refused`.
issues.title: Two of the three new negative wiring assertions ship without the positive control the actionlint one got

verdict.summary:
The core fix is real and well-motivated: registry_selftest_gate previously derived its suite, its dependency table and its actionlint pin from SCRIPT_DIR (the ORCHESTRATOR revision) while grading a candidate checkout at PWD, so `run_enrolled_selftest` executed the orchestrator's unchanged scripts and the gate was effectively vacuous for the diff under test. Sourcing the candidate's worker-live.sh is correctly avoided (_selftest_env_requirements_from_script PARSES it, refusing missing/duplicated/unterminated/empty tables), the actionlint override is confined to a command-substitution subshell and only redirects the pin PATH (host/path template and both digest checks are untouched, and pr-gate.yml already read the PR tree's scripts/actionlint.pin, so the lanes now agree rather than diverge). The dispatch exact-block pin and every pre-existing #824/#524/#1575 wiring assertion were updated consistently and remain non-vacuous, and the new reader unit tests are genuine (they flip red on a wrong answer).

What blocks: making the requirement table candidate-controlled routes attacker-controlled text into an OLD sink — `_selftest_dep_present pymodule` runs `python3 -c ... importlib.util.find_spec(sys.argv[1])` with cwd = the candidate tree root. A dotted probe name makes find_spec IMPORT the parent package, and for `python3 -c` sys.path[0] is the cwd, so a candidate that ships a top-level package plus one table row gets code execution in the worker lane BEFORE the suite and entirely OUTSIDE run_enrolled_selftest's gh shim — the lane this file documents as running with ambient `gh` credentials. The new reader applies no row-shape validation at all, so nothing else constrains the probe. That defeats the very property the change's own comment claims ('sourcing ... would execute the change before the sandboxed suite').
